assumptions: CONFIG ENDPOINT (fork resolved to recommended default; user to confirm): the spec §1 + AC#7 mention GET /me/config, which does NOT exist in the codebase. We add a dedicated GET /geo/config (anonymous + X-Fleet-Slug, mirroring the existing anonymous GET /public/fleet) carrying browser key + tile template + attribution + map center/zoom. AC#7's key-leak scan targets /geo/config and /public/fleet. No /me/config is created.

AC#3 ETA GATING (fork resolved): SignalR exposes no native group-membership count, so the driver->pickup ETA refresh throttle (<=60s, gated on an active viewer of order:{id} or the dispatcher detail) needs a custom subscriber-tracker or an order.LastEtaRefreshAt + viewer-count heuristic. It gets its own backend WI (WI-11), flagged needs_library_research, so the impl agent designs the tracking mechanism. The create-time single quote call lives separately in WI-10.

WI GRANULARITY (fork resolved): budget-alert + cache-cleanup TTL sweep are merged into one geo-jobs WI (WI-13). §7 doc edits are distributed onto their motivating code WIs (decisions.md->WI-01; costs.md + runbook->WI-13/WI-18); a thin AC#8 docs WI (WI-18) covers 00-PROJECT-CONTEXT + assignments 02/04/06/08 and confirms the decisions.md/costs.md entries exist.

Circuit breaker uses Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience 10.x (verified .NET 10-compatible on nuget.org, 2026). WI-01 verifies the exact pinned version and records docs/decisions.md; if a version conflict with the EF pin surfaces, WI-01 falls back to a ~40-line DelegatingHandler breaker exposing IsOpen.

The geo seam evolves into two Infrastructure/Geo/ layers: IMapyClient (low-level typed HttpClient + resilience + server key) and IGeoService (high-level cache->client->degradation orchestration, successor to IGeoProvider). QuoteEndpoint calls the provider IN-PROCESS (not HTTP), so it is repointed to IGeoService, not to an HTTP call.
Demo/first-day fleets use env fallback keys (Mapy__ServerKey/Mapy__BrowserKey); DevelopmentSeeder writes NO encrypted key columns (leaves them null) and TaxiDbContextFactory/seeder stay untouched.

Encrypted keys use IDataProtectionProvider via a Common/ IFleetKeyProtector (NOT an EF ValueConverter, which would break the design-time factory). AddDataProtection().PersistKeysToFileSystem(<mounted volume>).SetApplicationName("taxi") is MANDATORY — without a persisted key-ring the stored fleet keys become permanently undecryptable on restart. Persistence is enforced two ways, not by a runbook note alone: (1) PRIMARY — a fail-fast DataProtectionKeyRingGuard in WI-03 refuses to boot in non-Development when the keys dir is ephemeral/non-persistent; (2) a persistent named keys volume mounted onto the api service in the infra compose (WI-18).

geo_cache and geo_usage are NOT ITenantEntity (no query filter) — read from varied scopes incl background jobs, mirroring the RefreshToken/SmsCode no-filter decision. Explicit Where(c => c.FleetId == .. && ..) instead.

GeoResult is a discriminated result union (Success | Unavailable); the client boundary maps 4s-timeout / retry-exhausted-5xx / breaker-open to Unavailable (sanctioned log-and-continue carve-out of rules/error-handling.md). Endpoints guard-clause on the result — no handler try/catch, never null.

The customer-facing "orientacni odhad"/wider +-20% band (AC#5) is a RESPONSE-BODY estimate-mode field, NOT the debug X-Geo-* header. X-Geo-Source/X-Geo-Cache are debug-only headers on the 4 proxy endpoints; /geo/config uses Cache-Control max-age instead.

work_items.title: Geo schema — fleet_settings + orders columns, geo_cache, geo_usage entities + migration
acceptance_criteria: fleet_settings gains MapyServerKey string? (text, HasMaxLength(512), holds protected base64), MapyBrowserKey string? (same), MapCenterLat double (HasDefaultValue 50.08), MapCenterLng double (HasDefaultValue 14.42), MapZoom int (HasDefaultValue 12), GeoMonthlyCreditBudget int (HasDefaultValue 250000). Every NON-NULL new column MUST have HasDefaultValue (backfill on the populated table). XML-doc each property; keys are never logged.
orders gains DistanceM int? and DurationS int? (nullable -> metadata-only ADD COLUMN, no table rewrite, no index). XML-doc each.

GeoCacheEntry entity: composite PK (FleetId, Kind, Key) which IS the lookup index (no separate index); Kind is a C# enum GeoCacheKind{Suggest,Geocode,Reverse,Route,QuickPlace} (enum-as-string, HasMaxLength on the string PK col); Value JsonDocument? .HasColumnType("jsonb"); CreatedAt DateTimeOffset with HasIndex for the TTL sweep; cascade FK to Fleet; NOT ITenantEntity and NO query filter; DbSet registered.

GeoUsage entity: composite PK (FleetId, Day, Kind) with Day DateOnly (date column); Calls int; CreditsEst int; NOT ITenantEntity / no query filter; PK covers monthly aggregation (WHERE fleet_id=.. AND day>=monthStart AND day<monthEnd GROUP BY); DbSet registered.

Migration AddMapyGeoSchema created with --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations from api/src/Taxi.Api; generated SQL is additive-only (ADD COLUMN + CREATE TABLE, no drops/renames, no index on orders); a test applies it against Testcontainers Postgres and asserts the geo_cache composite PK uniqueness + geo_usage upsert PK.
TaxiDbContextFactory (NullCurrentTenant) still constructs the context at design time (no EF ValueConverter on the key columns).

work_items.title: IFleetKeyProtector + DataProtection wiring (persisted key-ring)
acceptance_criteria: IFleetKeyProtector { string Protect(string plaintext); string Unprotect(string ciphertext); } in Common/Security/, implemented over IDataProtectionProvider.CreateProtector("FleetSettings.MapyKeys"). Round-trip test: Unprotect(Protect(x)) == x.

Program.cs registers AddDataProtection().PersistKeysToFileSystem(<configured keys dir>).SetApplicationName("taxi") — the persisted key-ring is MANDATORY (without it stored fleet keys become permanently undecryptable on restart). The keys directory path comes from configuration (env/volume mount) with a sensible local default.
A test proves two protectors built from the SAME persisted key-ring directory can decrypt each other's ciphertext (simulating a restart); protectors from different app-names/rings cannot.
Keys are never logged (verified by the logging rule); the columns stay plain nullable text holding base64 ciphertext (no EF ValueConverter).

PRIMARY persistence safeguard: a DataProtectionKeyRingGuard fails-fast at startup (throws before the app boots) when the configured keys directory is non-persistent/ephemeral — missing, unwritable, or pointing at a container-ephemeral path (e.g. the default temp/app-local dir when a persistent volume mount is expected). A redeploy without a persistent ring makes every stored fleet Mapy key permanently undecryptable, so the app MUST refuse to boot rather than silently mint a throwaway ring. In Development the guard is relaxed to allow the sensible local default dir; in non-Development it requires an explicitly configured persistent path.

The Docker keys-volume mount is ALSO captured as a note for the ops runbook (delivered in WI-18/§8) and as a concrete mounted-keys volume in the infra compose (delivered in WI-18) — the startup guard is the primary safeguard, the mounted volume is the deployment provision.

work_items.title: IMapyClient typed HttpClient + resilience/breaker + HttpMessageHandler test seam
acceptance_criteria: IMapyClient exposes typed methods for /v1/suggest, /v1/geocode, /v1/rgeocode, /v1/routing/route, each returning a GeoResult<T> discriminated union (Success(value) | Unavailable(reason)) — never throws for degradation, never returns null.

MapyClient is a typed HttpClient registered in GeoFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies with a resilience pipeline: 4s timeout, 1 retry on 5xx, circuit breaker after 5 failures / 30s with half-open probes; breaker-open is queryable and short-circuits (no upstream call, no credit spent). The old photon/osrm named clients are removed.

The server key is resolved per-fleet via MapyKeyResolver (Unprotect(fleet.MapyServerKey) else env Mapy__ServerKey fallback) and attached to every Mapy call; the key is never logged (log templates use event phrases only).
try/catch for infra (timeout, retry-exhausted 5xx, breaker-open) lives INSIDE MapyClient and maps to GeoResult.Unavailable there (the sanctioned degradation carve-out).

A REAL MapyClient over a stubbed HttpMessageHandler (ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler / StubMapyHttpHandler) proves: (a) a 200 maps to Success with parsed street+municipality+lat+lng; (b) five consecutive 503s open the breaker and the sixth call returns Unavailable WITHOUT hitting the handler (assert on the handler's call counter); (c) the request URL carries type=regional.address,regional.street,poi and lang=cs for suggest.

work_items.title: Common/Geo pure helpers — cache-key folding/rounding, haversine, ETA fallback
acceptance_criteria: GeoCacheKey: pure folding — suggest key = lowercased+trimmed+diacritics-folded q + near rounded to 2 decimals; geocode = folded q; reverse = lat,lng at 4 decimals; route = from+to at 4 decimals. Deterministic and tested for diacritics ("Nadrazi" == "nadrazi").
HaversineDistance.Meters(lat1,lng1,lat2,lng2) returns great-circle metres; a known Prague pair matches an expected value within tolerance.
GeoEstimateFallback: distance = haversine x 1.3 road factor; ETA = distanceM / (35 km/h); the +-20% band bounds are pure functions. All covered by unit tests.
All helpers are pure static (no DI, no I/O) beside ZoneBbox.cs per architecture#common-infrastructure.

work_items.title: GeoCache two-tier (MemoryCache L1 + Postgres L2) + geo_usage accounting
acceptance_criteria: GeoCache is SCOPED (composes singleton IMemoryCache L1 + scoped TaxiDbContext L2 + TimeProvider) — a singleton capturing DbContext would be a captive-dependency bug; the WI proves the registration lifetime is scoped.

Read path: L1 hit -> return; L1 miss + L2 hit (and CreatedAt + ttlForKind >= now) -> hydrate L1 + return; else miss. TTL is app-enforced per kind (suggest 7d, geocode 30d, reverse 30d, route 24h, quickplace forever) — a stale L2 row is treated as a miss. jsonb Value is loaded then read (RootElement), never projected in a Select.

GeoUsageRecorder increments geo_usage via an ATOMIC INSERT..ON CONFLICT (fleet_id,day,kind) DO UPDATE SET calls=geo_usage.calls+EXCLUDED.calls, credits_est=geo_usage.credits_est+EXCLUDED.credits_est using ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync (NOT read-modify-write — concurrent misses must not race). A concurrent-misses test asserts the final count equals the number of misses.

Accounting is caller-driven (the single accounting site is the cache-miss in WI-07's IGeoService, not a decorator): +4 credits per suggest/geocode/reverse/route miss. GeoCache itself does not increment on hit or on breaker-open.
A test proves: two identical reads -> first is a miss (writes L1+L2), second is an L1 hit with no L2 query and no usage increment.

work_items.title: IGeoService orchestration (cache->client->degradation) + high-level test fake
acceptance_criteria: IGeoService high-level surface (Suggest/Geocode/Reverse/Route + a QuickPlace lookup that never calls Mapy) composes cache -> client -> degradation and returns a result carrying a source/cache/degraded signal so endpoints can set X-Geo-* headers and the estimate-mode body field. Successor to IGeoProvider; PhotonOsrmGeoProvider and the old IGeoProvider are deleted.

On cache miss: call IMapyClient; on Success -> write L1+L2, increment geo_usage +4 (the single accounting site), signal cache=miss/source=mapy; on Unavailable (breaker-open/timeout/5xx) -> NO usage increment, return a degraded result (haversine x1.3 / ETA fallback for route, empty for suggest, coords-only for reverse).

A high-level FakeGeoService (successor to FakeGeoProvider, carrying the shared-singleton Reset() discipline: Reset() FIRST then set fields) is wired into TaxiApiFactory and used by most integration tests; it can be told to return Unavailable to drive AC#5 degradation without a real HTTP stub.

GeoServiceTests prove: cache-hit path spends no credit and does not call the client; Unavailable route returns the haversine x1.3 estimate with the wider band flagged; QuickPlace lookup never touches the client or usage.
QuoteEndpoint and the Geo endpoints compile against IGeoService (the swap itself is completed in WI-08/WI-09/WI-10).

SuggestItemDto grows to (Label, Street?, Municipality?, Lat, Lng) so "Kollarova" and "nadrazi Kolin" return street+town. Upstream Unavailable -> 200 empty (never 502). A second identical query returns X-Geo-Cache: hit with no client call.

work_items.title: Pricing/Quote on IGeoService + persist order DistanceM/DurationS (quote-once)
acceptance_criteria: QuoteEndpoint injects IGeoService (not IGeoProvider); on a known dropoff it calls Route once; on GeoResult.Unavailable it no longer 502s — it falls back to the haversine x1.3 estimate with a WIDER +-20% band and an estimate-mode = "orientacni odhad" body field (AC#5); a matched Fixed route still short-circuits with zero geo calls.

The Estimate quote result carries DistanceM/DurationS so the order-create path persists them onto the order (DistanceM, DurationS) — the create-time route call happens at most once (AC#3 first clause).
A test with the fake returning Unavailable proves an order can still be created with the wider-band estimate and "orientacni odhad" label; a happy-path test proves exactly one route call at create.
geo_usage reflects the create-time miss only (no double counting).

work_items.title: Driver->pickup ETA — accept-time single call + throttled viewer-gated refresh
acceptance_criteria: SCOUT FIRST (why needs_library_research): SignalR exposes no native group-member count. The impl agent must design a viewer-tracking mechanism — an OrderSubscriptionTracker (in-memory count incremented in FleetHub.Subscribe / decremented in OnDisconnectedAsync for order:{id}, plus a dispatcher-detail-open signal) — and confirm it is queryable from the ETA refresh path. Document the chosen mechanism in the WI notes.

OrderSubscriptionTracker is an in-memory singleton (mirrors the DriverPositionStore precedent) — it MUST be DI-registered with singleton lifetime and reset per-test (shared across the test collection, so tests must clear/reset it to avoid cross-test leakage exactly like FakeGeoProvider/DriverPositionStore).
On Accept: exactly one route call computes the initial driver->pickup ETA (AC#3 second clause). Assigning + accepting together cause at most one more route call beyond create.

While at least one viewer is subscribed to order:{id} (or the dispatcher has the detail open), the ETA refreshes at most every 60s -> a customer watching for 5 minutes causes <= 5 further route calls; nobody watching -> 0 calls, and between refreshes the ETA is EXTRAPOLATED from remaining distance and last average speed (no API call).
The dispatcher board assign-picker driver->pickup distances use haversine only (no API call) — verified: opening the picker triggers zero route calls.
PickupEtaTests (using the fake geo service + a controllable TimeProvider + a controllable subscriber tracker) assert the call-count bounds for: create=1, accept=+1, 5-min watch<=5, no-watcher=0.

work_items.title: Geo usage settings read + 80%/100% budget alert via notification engine
acceptance_criteria: A settings read endpoint (GET /settings/geo-usage) uses Policies(nameof(AuthorizationPolicies.FleetAdminOnly)) — the settings/budget page is a FleetAdmin surface, so the single concrete policy is FleetAdminOnly (NOT DispatcherOnly). It returns this month's estimated credits + % of GeoMonthlyCreditBudget for the current fleet (plain-LINQ GroupBy over geo_usage WHERE fleet_id AND day in [monthStart,monthEnd) — no SqlQuery aliasing needed on read).

When a cache-miss upsert crosses 80% or 100% of GeoMonthlyCreditBudget for the fleet-month, a FleetAdmin alert is enqueued via the notification engine (new NotificationEvent member, e.g. GeoBudgetWarning) and a notification_log row is written; each threshold fires at most once per fleet-month (dedup on the existing NotificationLog unique index shape).

A test with GeoMonthlyCreditBudget = 100 credits proves the 80% alert fires exactly once when usage crosses 80 (AC#6); usage below threshold fires nothing; a further miss that keeps usage in the 80-100% band does NOT re-fire the 80% alert (dedup per fleet + ISO-month).

A test proves the 100% alert fires exactly once when usage crosses 100% of GeoMonthlyCreditBudget (AC#6 requires alerts at BOTH 80% and 100%); an already-sent 100% alert is not re-fired on subsequent misses in the same fleet-month.
geo_usage reflects cache MISSES only (verified: a cache-hit read does not move the counter).
SeedAndEndToEndTests allowlist + docs/api.md updated for the new settings endpoint (depends_on WI-09 serializes the shared-file edits).

work_items.title: Geo background jobs — cache TTL cleanup sweep + costs.md measurement note
acceptance_criteria: GeoCacheCleanupJob follows the RunTickAsync PeriodicTimer shell (internal RunTickAsync(ct) with all logic; ExecuteAsync a thin timer shell) and is registered in JobsServiceExtensions.AddJobs().

Per tick it ExecuteDeleteAsync's expired geo_cache rows per-kind (CreatedAt + ttlForKind < now) EXCEPT QuickPlace (forever — cleanup skips it; QuickPlace invalidation happens on Place edit, not here).
A test seeds cache rows of each kind at varying ages, constructs the job and calls RunTickAsync directly (advancing FakeTimeProvider), and asserts only the expired non-QuickPlace rows are deleted.

A cross-fleet test (fleet A + fleet B usage) proves the SuperAdmin sees both fleets' rows; a non-SuperAdmin gets 403.
